question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Degron depletion after priming
ideas.description: Prime cells with a transient stimulus, then acutely degrade FOS/JUN (dTAG/AID) before re-stimulation. If enhanced response and accessibility persist without AP-1, memory is held elsewhere. If they collapse, AP-1 is required for maintenance.

ideas.title: Optogenetic AP-1 pulse-and-probe
ideas.description: Use light-controlled AP-1 activation with defined pulse number, amplitude, and interval, then re-stimulate after variable delays. Measure the response and decay half-life to test sufficiency, dose-dependence, and hysteresis of memory without other signaling inputs.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome with lineage barcodes
ideas.description: Do paired RNA+ATAC on primed and naive cells with heritable barcodes to track clones across divisions. Test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are clonally inherited and whether they predict individual cells' re-stimulation response.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and residence-time measurements
ideas.description: Combine live-cell single-molecule tracking and CUT&RUN on mitotic-arrested cells to measure whether FOS/JUN stay bound at primed enhancers through mitosis. Compare residence times in primed vs naive cells to show stable, heritable binding.

ideas.title: Motif-specific enhancer editing and forced recruitment
ideas.description: CRISPR-mutate AP-1 motifs at persistently accessible enhancers to test necessity, and use dCas9-FOS/JUN to recruit AP-1 to naive loci to test sufficiency. Read out the kinetics of re-stimulation, accessibility, and H3K27ac, separating AP-1 from other chromatin-based memory.

candidates: Time-course ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy before, during, and after transient stimulus
Acute degron depletion of AP-1 (e.g., JUN/FOS dTAG) after stimulus to test if memory persists without AP-1
Single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) tracking primed vs naive cells and AP-1 motif accessibility
Optogenetic pulses of AP-1 activation with varying dose/timing, reading out later re-stimulation response
Live-cell reporters of FOS/JUN dynamics with lineage tracing across divisions
Mitotic bookmarking assay: AP-1 retention on mitotic chromosomes by live imaging and CUT&RUN
Mutate AP-1 motifs at specific memory enhancers by CRISPR and test re-stimulation kinetics
dCas9-based forced AP-1 recruitment to a locus to test sufficiency of memory
Hi-C / Micro-C of enhancer-promoter contacts before/after priming and AP-1 loss
Histone mark (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) ChIP time course to separate AP-1 from chromatin-mediated memory
Pharmacologic JNK/MAPK inhibition during the memory window versus during priming
Mathematical modeling of AP-1 feedback loops to predict bistability and hysteresis
Single-molecule tracking of FOS/JUN residence times on chromatin in primed vs naive cells
Proteomics of AP-1 dimer composition shifts (FOS vs FOSL, JUN family) after stimulus
Epidermal/stem cell in vivo wound-memory model with AP-1 inhibition (e.g., dominant-negative A-FOS)
Compare AP-1 memory across cell types using public ATAC datasets for stimulus-induced persistent sites
Pioneer-factor cooperativity tests: AP-1 with BAF/SWI-SNF inhibition on persistent accessibility
Nucleosome positioning (MNase/footprinting) at persistent AP-1 sites
Cell-division dependence: block division vs allow, measure memory decay half-life
Transgenerational / long-term decay measurement of primed state with CRISPR-based AP-1 barcoded sorting
